title: The Last Veil
premise: Isandro Vasquez, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a ledger-keeper for the Veiled Exchange—a guild that trades in impossible things—has spent a decade erasing every trace of their gift. When the crown's Veilhunt begins and guild members start vanishing, Isandro discovers their own name was sold to the hunters by someone inside the Exchange. Fleeing with a stolen ledger that proves the crown's magic was built on a broken covenant between realms, Isandro gathers scattered gift-bearers to reforge that covenant at the Standing Stones before the long winter seals the veil forever. They succeed at terrible cost—sacrificing their own memories of belonging—but end the book choosing to rebuild those memories alongside a found family, no longer hidden.
about_author: Kestrel Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city's forgotten records wing. They write fantasy about people the histories tried to erase, and they still cannot sleep through thunderstorms.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dry Ink
chapters.summary: Isandro Vasquez catalogs impossible trades for the Veiled Exchange: bottled echoes, borrowed shadows, one last summer. Their storm-calling stays buried beneath ledgers and routine. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility, and the first hairline crack—a client's payment hums with familiar storm-light.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Every Square
chapters.summary: Criers announce the Veilhunt: all gift-bearers must register or be taken. The Exchange's mistress, Odile Ferran, orders everyone to keep working and keep quiet. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread settling into the bones; Isandro realizes the guild's neutrality is a story they've been telling themselves.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Names
chapters.summary: A hooded buyer purchases a rare memory-wipe and pays partly in names—including, Isandro notices later, three registered gift-bearers. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into suspicion; the hunt has found a door into the guild itself.

chapters.title: What Odile Keeps Below
chapters.summary: Investigating the vault, Isandro finds a sealed covenant-stone fragment and records showing the Exchange once served as keeper of the pact between human and elderkin realms. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: awe and betrayal intertwined—the guild was never neutral, only amnesiac by design.

chapters.title: The First Vanishing
chapters.summary: Fellow ledger-clerk Sefa is dragged from her cot by masked hunters. Isandro does nothing, and the silence afterward is louder than any storm. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: shame as a turning point; staying invisible now means complicity.

chapters.title: Thunder Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Hunters sweep the Exchange. Cornered, Isandro's control slips—a window shatters, rain bends sideways—and they escape through the flooded undercity with the stolen covenant-ledger. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; the gift, so long caged, answers like an old friend.

chapters.title: The Drowned Market
chapters.summary: In the sunken market quarter, Isandro meets Rook, a smuggler who moves gift-bearers out of the city, and Tam, a child who hears doors before they open. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: wary connection; strangers becoming the beginnings of a crew.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Broken Pact
chapters.summary: Deciphering the stolen ledger, Isandro learns the crown's own authority derives from the covenant—which was shattered deliberately two generations ago to hoard magic for the throne. POV: alternating Isandro and Rook. Emotional beat: righteous fury; justice outside the law starts here.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: Veilhunter Captain Aurel Vane corners them but hesitates—he grew up beside a storm-caller he was made to forget. He lets them go, marking himself a traitor. POV: Aurel. Emotional beat: a hunter's crisis of conscience; memory as resistance.

chapters.title: North Through the Falling White
chapters.summary: The company flees toward the Standing Stones ahead of the unnatural long winter. Cold kills one of Rook's runners; Tam blames Isandro's hesitation. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief and friction; belonging must be earned, not assumed.

chapters.title: The Elderkin Tollhouse
chapters.summary: At a border tollhouse, the elderkin gatekeeper Wren demands a price: a true memory freely given. Isandro pays with the recollection of their mother's face. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: sacrifice establishing stakes—reforging the covenant will cost exactly this kind of coin.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Captured Odile, transported as a prisoner, reveals she sold Isandro's name to buy the guild time—and that the Exchange's founders erased their own memories to survive the last betrayal. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: moral complexity; even betrayers are keeping their own ledgers.

chapters.title: The Storm That Learned Its Name
chapters.summary: Ambushed on a frozen pass, Isandro calls a true storm for the first time in ten years, saving the company but leveling the ridge. Tam watches, awed and afraid. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: power reclaimed, identity no longer deniable—but at what cost to others?

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Captain Vane catches up again, this time alone, offering his hunters' route-maps in exchange for a place in the reforging. Rook wants him dead; Isandro vouches. POV: Aurel. Emotional beat: trust extended across enemy lines; the covenant begins with people, not stones.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Passing through a town where the crown's memory-tithe emptied every mind of its history, the company sees the future the long winter promises. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: horror sharpening resolve; this is what losing memory truly means.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hearthline
chapters.summary: One of Rook's runners sells their position to save his registered sister. Hunters descend; Odile dies holding the pass so the others can run. POV: the runner, briefly, then Isandro. Emotional beat: devastating ambiguity—betrayal and love in the same hands.

chapters.title: The Standing Stones Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: They reach the Stones, half-buried in glacier. The ritual requires voices from both realms and a keeper willing to anchor it with their own memories of belonging. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: solemn clarity; Isandro understands the price and steps forward anyway.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Edge
chapters.summary: As the ritual begins, the crown's full hunting force arrives, led by the hooded buyer revealed as the King's Memory-Warden—the original covenant-breaker's heir. Battle erupts across the ice. POV: Aurel. Emotional beat: chaos and courage; allies hold lines they'd have fled a month ago.

chapters.title: Reforge
chapters.summary: At the heart of the storm, Isandro speaks the old words, gives up every memory of home and family and the Exchange, and binds the realms together. The winter breaks. Vane cuts down the Warden. POV: Isandro, fragmenting. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss; the climax paid in full.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Isandro wakes with no past, surrounded by strangers who grieve and celebrate at once. Rook begins reading aloud from the ledger Isandro kept of their own journey. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: tenderness; memory can be witnessed back into existence.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the company establishes a free haven at the Stones where gift-bearers register with no one but each other. Isandro, relearning themselves, chooses to stay—not from exile, but invitation. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: quiet rebuilding; belonging chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: First Thunder of Spring
chapters.summary: Spring's first storm rolls over the valley. Isandro stands in it, arms open, calling lightning not to hide but to greet it—while Tam laughs and the new community watches without fear. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: resolution and hope; the veil is lifted, and they are finally, fully seen.
